verdict.rationale: Sketch ships a built-in local MCP server that lets AI clients interact directly with Sketch. Its AI page says an AI client can "recreate text styles, colors, UI components, and even entire pages inside Sketch" and can sort, rename and align layers, which are write operations. It also offers an official JavaScript plugin API, and community posts describe a robust plugin ecosystem. Missing for 10: a documented list of MCP write tools and their limits (the server is local-only), and independent hands-on corroboration that agent-driven create or modify actions work as claimed.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can create or modify designs programmatically — through a write-capable API, plugin surface, or MCP tools — not just read them

citations.quote: Sketch includes a built-in MCP Server, a lightweight local-only web server that lets AI clients like ChatGPT or Claude interact directly with Sketch.
Point your AI client at a repo to recreate text styles, colors, UI components, and even entire pages inside Sketch.
Sort, rename, and align layers automatically.
Write a Sketch plugin in JavaScript. Take advantage of ES6, access macOS frameworks and use the Sketch APIs without learning Objective-C or Swift.
An official vanilla JavaScript API, fully supported between releases.
